sanskrit: sa hatvā saindhavaṃ saṃkhye punar etu dhanaṃjayaḥ jitvā ripugaṇāṃś caiva pārayatv arjuno vratam
english: "May Dhanaṃjaya, when he has slain the Saindhava in battle, return again to us; and having vanquished the hosts of his foes, may Arjuna fulfill his vow."

sanskrit: ahatvā sindhurājaṃ hi dhūmaketuṃ pravekṣyati na hy etad anṛtaṃ kartum arhaḥ pārtho dhanaṃjayaḥ
english: "For if he does not slay the king of the Sindhus, he will enter the smoke-bannered fire; yet Pārtha Dhanaṃjaya is not one to let his word prove false."

sanskrit: dharmaputraḥ kathaṃ rājā bhaviṣyati mṛte 'rjune tasmin hi vijayaḥ kṛtsnaḥ pāṇḍavena samāhitaḥ
english: "How shall the king, the son of Dharma, fare if Arjuna dies? For upon him alone has the Pāṇḍava rested the whole of his hope of victory."

sanskrit: yadi naḥ sukṛtaṃ kiṃ cid yadi dattaṃ hutaṃ yadi phalena tasya sarvasya savyasācī jayatv arīn
english: "If we have done any good deed, if we have given gifts or made oblation, then by the fruit of all of that may Savyasācin conquer his enemies."

sanskrit: evaṃ kathayatāṃ teṣāṃ jayam āśaṃsatāṃ prabho kṛcchreṇa mahatā rājan rajanī vyatyavartata
english: As they spoke thus, O lord, longing for his victory, the night passed away, O king, only with the greatest difficulty.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ rajanyāṃ madhye tu pratibuddho janārdanaḥ smṛtvā pratijñāṃ pārthasya dārukaṃ pratyabhāṣata
english: In the middle of that night Janārdana awoke, and remembering the vow of Pārtha, he spoke thus to Dāruka:

sanskrit: arjunena pratijñātam ārtena hatabandhunā jayadrathaṃ haniṣyāmi śvobhūta iti dāruka
english: "Arjuna, stricken with grief at the slaying of his kinsman, has vowed, O Dāruka: 'I shall slay Jayadratha when tomorrow has come.'"

sanskrit: tat tu duryodhanaḥ śrutvā mantribhir mantrayiṣyati yathā jayadrathaṃ pārtho na hanyād iti saṃyuge
english: "When Duryodhana hears of this, he will take counsel with his ministers, so that Pārtha may not slay Jayadratha in the fight."

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyo hi tāḥ sarvā rakṣiṣyanti jayadratham droṇaś ca saha putreṇa sarvāstravidhipāragaḥ
english: "All those armies in their full array will guard Jayadratha, and so too will Droṇa with his son, who is master of every science of arms."

sanskrit: eko vīraḥ sahasrākṣo daityadānavamarditā so 'pi taṃ notsahetājau hantuṃ droṇena rakṣitam
english: "Even the thousand-eyed one, the lone hero who crushes the Daityas and Dānavas, could not bring himself to slay him in battle when he is guarded by Droṇa."

sanskrit: so 'haṃ śvas tat kariṣyāmi yathā kuntīsuto 'rjunaḥ aprāpte 'staṃ dinakare haniṣyati jayadratham
english: "Therefore tomorrow I shall so contrive it that Arjuna, the son of Kuntī, shall slay Jayadratha before the sun reaches its setting."

sanskrit: na hi dārā na mitrāṇi jñātayo na ca bāndhavāḥ kaś cin nānyaḥ priyataraḥ kuntīputrān mamārjunāt
english: "For not my wives, nor friends, nor kinsmen, nor any other dearer to me than the son of Kuntī—none is there dearer to me than Arjuna."

sanskrit: anarjunam imaṃ lokaṃ muhūrtam api dāruka udīkṣituṃ na śakto 'haṃ bhavitā na ca tat tathā
english: "A world without Arjuna I could not bear to look upon even for a moment, O Dāruka; nor shall it ever come to be so."

sanskrit: ahaṃ dhvajinyaḥ śatrūṇāṃ sahayāḥ sarathadvipāḥ arjunārthe haniṣyāmi sakarṇāḥ sasuyodhanāḥ
english: "For Arjuna's sake I shall destroy the bannered hosts of the foe, with their horses, chariots, and elephants, together with Karṇa and Suyodhana themselves."

sanskrit: śvo nirīkṣantu me vīryaṃ trayo lokā mahāhave dhanaṃjayārthaṃ samare parākrāntasya dāruka
english: "Tomorrow let the three worlds behold my prowess in the great battle, O Dāruka, as I exert myself in the fray for the sake of Dhanaṃjaya."

sanskrit: śvo narendrasahasrāṇi rājaputraśatāni ca sāśvadviparathāny ājau vidraviṣyanti dāruka
english: "Tomorrow thousands of kings and hundreds of princes, with their horses, elephants, and chariots, shall flee before me in battle, O Dāruka."

sanskrit: śvas tāṃ cakrapramathitāṃ drakṣyase nṛpavāhinīm mayā kruddhena samare pāṇḍavārthe nipātitām
english: "Tomorrow you shall see the host of kings crushed by my discus, struck down in battle by me in my wrath for the Pāṇḍava's sake."

sanskrit: śvaḥ sadevāḥ sagandharvāḥ piśācoragarākṣasāḥ jñāsyanti lokāḥ sarve māṃ suhṛdaṃ savyasācinaḥ
english: "Tomorrow all the worlds, with their gods, Gandharvas, Piśācas, Uragas, and Rākṣasas, shall know me to be the friend of Savyasācin."

sanskrit: yas taṃ dveṣṭi sa māṃ dveṣṭi yas tam anu sa mām anu iti saṃkalpyatāṃ buddhyā śarīrārdhaṃ mamārjunaḥ
english: "Whoever hates him hates me; whoever follows him follows me. Let it be understood with certainty in your mind: Arjuna is the half of my own body."

sanskrit: yathā tvam aprabhātāyām asyāṃ niśi rathottamam kalpayitvā yathāśāstram ādāya vratasaṃyataḥ
english: "While this night has not yet given way to dawn, do you, bound to your duty, make ready and bring forth my best of chariots according to the rule,"

sanskrit: gadāṃ kaumodakīṃ divyāṃ śaktiṃ cakraṃ dhanuḥ śarān āropya vai rathe sūta sarvopakaraṇāni ca
english: "setting upon the chariot, O charioteer, the divine mace Kaumodakī, the spear, the discus, the bow and arrows, and all the other accoutrements as well."

sanskrit: sthānaṃ hi kalpayitvā ca rathopasthe dhvajasya me vainateyasya vīrasya samare rathaśobhinaḥ
english: "And having prepared upon the floor of the chariot a place for my banner—the heroic son of Vinatā, who graces the chariot in battle—"

sanskrit: chatraṃ jāmbūnadair jālair arkajvalanasaṃnibhaiḥ viśvakarmakṛtair divyair aśvān api ca bhūṣitān
english: "and the parasol with its nets of pure gold, bright as the sun and fire, fashioned by Viśvakarman, divine—and the horses, well adorned,"

sanskrit: balāhakaṃ meghapuṣpaṃ sainyaṃ sugrīvam eva ca yuktvā vājivarān yattaḥ kavacī tiṣṭha dāruka
english: "having yoked those best of steeds, Balāhaka, Meghapuṣpa, Saiṇya, and Sugrīva, stand ready and clad in armor, O Dāruka."

sanskrit: pāñcajanyasya nirghoṣam ārṣabheṇaiva pūritam śrutvā tu bhairavaṃ nādam upayāyā javena mām
english: "And when you hear the terrible blast of Pāñcajanya, filled with a deep bull-like note, come swiftly to me."

sanskrit: ekāhnāham amarṣaṃ ca sarvaduḥkhāni caiva ha bhrātuḥ pitṛṣvaseyasya vyapaneṣyāmi dāruka
english: "In a single day I shall sweep away all the indignation and all the sorrows of my cousin, the son of my father's sister, O Dāruka."

sanskrit: sarvopāyair yatiṣyāmi yathā bībhatsur āhave paśyatāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ haniṣyati jayadratham
english: "By every means I shall strive so that Bībhatsu may slay Jayadratha in the battle before the very eyes of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra."

sanskrit: yasya yasya ca bībhatsur vadhe yatnaṃ kariṣyati āśaṃse sārathe tatra bhavitāsya dhruvo jayaḥ
english: "And against whomsoever Bībhatsu shall make his effort to slay, there, O charioteer, I am sure his victory is assured."

sanskrit: dāruka uvāca jaya eva dhruvas tasya kuta eva parājayaḥ yasya tvaṃ puruṣavyāghra sārathyam upajagmivān
english: Dāruka said: "Victory indeed is assured to him—how could there ever be defeat for one whose charioteer you have become, O tiger among men?"

sanskrit: evaṃ caitat kariṣyāmi yathā mām anuśāsasi suprabhātām imāṃ rātriṃ jayāya vijayasya hi
english: "And I shall do all this just as you command me, that this night may break in fair dawn for the victory of Vijaya."

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca kuntīputras tu taṃ mantraṃ smarann eva dhanaṃjayaḥ pratijñām ātmano rakṣan mumohācintyavikramaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: But the son of Kuntī, Dhanaṃjaya of inconceivable valor, even as he brooded upon that resolve and guarded his own vow, was overcome with bewilderment.

sanskrit: taṃ tu śokena saṃtaptaṃ svapne kapivaradhvajam āsasāda mahātejā dhyāyantaṃ garuḍadhvajaḥ
english: As he, the hero of the monkey banner, lay consumed with grief and lost in thought, the one of mighty splendor, he of the Garuḍa banner, came to him in a dream.

sanskrit: pratyutthānaṃ tu kṛṣṇasya sarvāvasthaṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ nālopayata dharmātmā bhaktyā premṇā ca sarvadā
english: In every circumstance Dhanaṃjaya, righteous of soul, never failed in rising to greet Kṛṣṇa, always out of devotion and love.

sanskrit: pratyutthāya ca govindaṃ sa tasmāy āsanaṃ dadau na cāsane svayaṃ buddhiṃ bībhatsur vyadadhāt tadā
english: And rising to greet Govinda, he gave him a seat; nor did Bībhatsu then set his own mind upon taking a seat himself.

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇo mahātejā jānan pārthasya niścayam kuntīputram idaṃ vākyam āsīnaḥ sthitam abravīt
english: Then Kṛṣṇa of great splendor, knowing the resolve of Pārtha, being seated, spoke these words to the son of Kuntī who stood before him:

sanskrit: mā viṣāde manaḥ pārtha kṛthāḥ kālo hi durjayaḥ kālaḥ sarvāṇi bhūtāni niyacchati pare vidhau
english: "Set not your mind upon despair, O Pārtha; for Time is hard to conquer. Time draws all beings on, into the supreme ordinance."

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ ca viṣādas te tad brūhi vadatāṃ vara na śocitavyaṃ viduṣā śokaḥ kāryavināśanaḥ
english: "And why this despair of yours? Tell me, O best of speakers. The wise man should not grieve, for grief is the ruin of every undertaking."

sanskrit: śocan nandayate śatrūn karśayaty api bāndhavān kśīyate ca naras tasmān na tvaṃ śocitum arhasi
english: "By grieving a man gladdens his enemies and wastes away his kinsmen, and is himself diminished. Therefore you ought not to grieve."

sanskrit: ity ukto vāsudevena bībhatsur aparājitaḥ ābabhāṣe tadā vidvān idaṃ vacanam arthavat
english: Thus addressed by Vāsudeva, the unconquered Bībhatsu, learned as he was, then spoke these meaningful words:

sanskrit: mayā pratijñā mahatī jayadrathavadhe kṛtā śvo 'smi hantā durātmānaṃ putraghnam iti keśava
english: "A mighty vow has been made by me concerning the slaying of Jayadratha—that 'tomorrow I shall slay that evil-souled killer of my son,' O Keśava."

sanskrit: matpratijñāvighātārthaṃ dhārtarāṣṭraiḥ kilācyuta pṛṣṭhataḥ saindhavaḥ kāryaḥ sarvair gupto mahārathaiḥ
english: "To thwart my vow, O Acyuta, the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra will surely keep the Saindhava in the rear, guarded by all their great chariot-warriors."

sanskrit: daśa caikā ca tāḥ kṛṣṇa akṣauhiṇyaḥ sudurjayāḥ pratijñāyāṃ ca hīnāyāṃ kathaṃ jīveta madvidhaḥ
english: "Eleven armies are theirs, O Kṛṣṇa, exceedingly hard to overcome; and should my vow fail, how could one such as I go on living?"

sanskrit: duḥkhopāyasya me vīra vikāṅkṣā parivartate drutaṃ ca yāti savitā tata etad bravīmy aham
english: "My longing, O hero, turns toward a thing whose accomplishment is fraught with hardship, and the sun moves swiftly on—therefore I say this to you."

sanskrit: śokasthānaṃ tu tac chrutvā pārthasya dvijaketanaḥ saṃspṛśyāmbhas tataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ prāṅmukhaḥ samavasthitaḥ
english: Having heard that ground of Pārtha's grief, Kṛṣṇa, whose emblem is the bird, touched water and then took his stand facing the east.

sanskrit: idaṃ vākyaṃ mahātejā babhāṣe puṣkarekṣaṇaḥ hitārthaṃ pāṇḍuputrasya saindhavasya vadhe vṛtaḥ
english: These words the lotus-eyed one of great splendor spoke, for the good of the son of Pāṇḍu, intent upon the slaying of the Saindhava:

sanskrit: pārtha pāśupataṃ nāma paramāstraṃ sanātanam yena sarvān mṛdhe daityāñ jaghne devo maheśvaraḥ
english: "O Pārtha, there is the supreme and eternal weapon called Pāśupata, with which the god Maheśvara slew all the Daityas in battle."

sanskrit: yadi tad viditaṃ te 'dya śvo hantāsi jayadratham atha jñātuṃ prapadyasva manasā vṛṣabhadhvajam
english: "If that weapon be known to you today, you shall slay Jayadratha tomorrow. But if you would learn it, take refuge in your mind with the god of the bull banner."

sanskrit: taṃ devaṃ manasā dhyāyañ joṣam āssva dhanaṃjaya tatas tasya prasādāt tvaṃ bhaktaḥ prāpsyasi tan mahat
english: "Meditating in your mind upon that god, remain in silence, O Dhanaṃjaya; then by his grace, being devoted, you shall obtain that mighty weapon."

sanskrit: tataḥ kṛṣṇavacaḥ śrutvā saṃspṛśyāmbho dhanaṃjayaḥ bhūmāv āsīna ekāgro jagāma manasā bhavam
english: Then, having heard the words of Kṛṣṇa, Dhanaṃjaya touched water and, seated upon the ground with single-pointed mind, went in thought to Bhava.

sanskrit: tataḥ praṇihite brāhme muhūrte śubhalakṣaṇe ātmānam arjuno 'paśyad gagane sahakeśavam
english: Then in the auspicious hour sacred to Brahmā, in that moment of fair omen, Arjuna beheld himself together with Keśava up in the sky.

sanskrit: jyotirbhiś ca samākīrṇaṃ siddhacāraṇasevitam vāyuvegagatiḥ pārthaḥ khaṃ bheje sahakeśavaḥ
english: And Pārtha, moving with the speed of the wind, together with Keśava, traversed the heaven, thronged with lights and frequented by Siddhas and Cāraṇas.

sanskrit: keśavena gṛhītaḥ sa dakṣiṇe vibhunā bhuje prekṣamāṇo bahūn bhāvāñ jagāmādbhutadarśanān
english: Held by the mighty Keśava upon his right arm, gazing upon many a wondrous form, he passed on through sights marvelous to behold.

sanskrit: udīcyāṃ diśi dharmātmā so 'paśyac chvetaparvatam kuberasya vihāre ca nalinīṃ padmabhūṣitām
english: In the northern quarter the righteous one beheld the White Mountain, and in Kubera's pleasure-grove a lotus-pool adorned with blossoms.

sanskrit: saricchreṣṭhāṃ ca tāṃ gaṅgāṃ vīkṣamāṇo bahūdakām sadāpuṣpaphalair vṛkṣair upetāṃ sphaṭikopalām
english: And he gazed upon the Gaṅgā, best of rivers, abounding in waters, set about with trees ever in flower and fruit, her stones of crystal,

sanskrit: siṃhavyāghrasamākīrṇāṃ nānāmṛgagaṇākulām puṇyāśramavatīṃ ramyāṃ manojñāṇḍajasevitām
english: thronged with lions and tigers, teeming with herds of many kinds of deer, holy with hermitages, lovely, and frequented by charming birds.

sanskrit: mandarasya pradeśāṃś ca kiṃnarodgītanāditān hemarūpyamayaiḥ śṛṅgair nānauṣadhividīpitān tathā mandāravṛkṣaiś ca puṣpitair upaśobhitān
english: And he beheld the regions of Mandara, resounding with the songs of Kiṃnaras, their peaks of gold and silver lit up by many healing herbs, and graced too with flowering coral trees.

sanskrit: snigdhāñjanacayākāraṃ saṃprāptaḥ kālaparvatam puṇyaṃ himavataḥ pādaṃ maṇimantaṃ ca parvatam brahmatuṅgaṃ nadīś cānyās tathā janapadān api
english: He reached the Kāla mountain, dark as a heap of glistening collyrium, the holy foothills of the Himavat, and Mount Maṇimat, and Brahmatuṅga, and other rivers as well, and the lands of men.

sanskrit: suśṛṅgaṃ śataśṛṅgaṃ ca śaryātivanam eva ca puṇyam aśvaśiraḥsthānaṃ sthānam ātharvaṇasya ca
english: And Suśṛṅga, and Śataśṛṅga, and the forest of Śaryāti, and the holy seat of the Horse's-Head, and the abode of Atharvaṇa.

sanskrit: vṛṣadaṃśaṃ ca śailendraṃ mahāmandaram eva ca apsarobhiḥ samākīrṇaṃ kiṃnaraiś copaśobhitam
english: And Vṛṣadaṃśa, lord of mountains, and great Mandara as well, thronged with Apsarases and made beautiful by Kiṃnaras.

sanskrit: tāṃś ca śailān vrajan pārthaḥ prekṣate sahakeśavaḥ śubhaiḥ prasravaṇair juṣṭān hemadhātuvibhūṣitān
english: And as he journeyed past those mountains, Pārtha, together with Keśava, gazed upon them, blessed with fair cascades and adorned with veins of gold.

sanskrit: candraraśmiprakāśāṅgīṃ pṛthivīṃ puramālinīm samudrāṃś cādbhutākārān apaśyad bahulākarān
english: He beheld the earth, her form gleaming as in moonbeams, garlanded with cities, and the oceans of wondrous aspect, abounding in rich stores of treasure.

sanskrit: viyad dyāṃ pṛthivīṃ caiva paśyan viṣṇupade vrajan vismitaḥ saha kṛṣṇena kṣipto bāṇa ivātyagāt
english: Gazing on the firmament, the heaven, and the earth, journeying through Viṣṇu's step, filled with wonder, he sped on with Kṛṣṇa, swift as an arrow loosed.

sanskrit: grahanakṣatrasomānāṃ sūryāgnyoś ca samatviṣam apaśyata tadā pārtho jvalantam iva parvatam
english: Then Pārtha beheld a mountain blazing as it were, of a radiance equal to that of the planets, the stars, the moon, the sun, and fire.

sanskrit: samāsādya tu taṃ śailaṃ śailāgre samavasthitam taponityaṃ mahātmānam apaśyad vṛṣabhadhvajam
english: And drawing near to that mountain, he beheld upon its summit the high-souled god of the bull banner, ever steadfast in austerity.

sanskrit: sahasram iva sūryāṇāṃ dīpyamānaṃ svatejasā śūlinaṃ jaṭilaṃ gauraṃ valkalājinavāsasam
english: He blazed with his own splendor like a thousand suns, bearing the trident, his hair matted, fair of hue, clad in bark and hide.

sanskrit: nayanānāṃ sahasraiś ca vicitrāṅgaṃ mahaujasam pārvatyā sahitaṃ devaṃ bhūtasaṃghaiś ca bhāsvaraiḥ
english: With his thousands of eyes, his body of marvelous form, of mighty power—the god, together with Pārvatī and with shining hosts of spirits—

sanskrit: gītavāditrasaṃhrādais tālalāsyasamanvitam valgitāsphoṭitotkruṣṭaiḥ puṇyagandhaiś ca sevitam
english: amid the swelling of song and instruments, attended by dance kept to the beat, by leaping and clapping and loud shouts, and served by holy fragrances.

sanskrit: stūyamānaṃ stavair divyair munibhir brahmavādibhiḥ goptāraṃ sarvabhūtānām iṣvāsadharam acyutam
english: He was being praised with divine hymns by sages who expound the Veda—the protector of all beings, bearer of the bow, the unfallen one.

sanskrit: vāsudevas tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā jagāma śirasā kṣitim pārthena saha dharmātmā gṛṇan brahma sanātanam
english: But Vāsudeva, beholding him, touched the earth with his head, together with Pārtha, the righteous one chanting the eternal sacred verse,

sanskrit: lokādiṃ viśvakarmāṇam ajam īśānam avyayam manasaḥ paramāṃ yoniṃ khaṃ vāyuṃ jyotiṣāṃ nidhim
english: hailing him as the origin of the worlds, the all-maker, the unborn, the lord, the imperishable, the supreme source of mind, the ether, the wind, the treasury of all lights,

sanskrit: sraṣṭāraṃ vāridhārāṇāṃ bhuvaś ca prakṛtiṃ parām devadānavayakṣāṇāṃ mānavānāṃ ca sādhanam
english: the creator of the streams of water, the supreme primal nature of the earth, the fulfiller of gods, Dānavas, Yakṣas, and men,

sanskrit: yogināṃ paramaṃ brahma vyaktaṃ brahmavidāṃ nidhim carācarasya sraṣṭāraṃ pratihartāram eva ca
english: the supreme Brahman of the yogins, made manifest, the treasure of those who know the Brahman, the creator of all that moves and is unmoving, and its destroyer too,

sanskrit: kālakopaṃ mahātmānaṃ śakrasūryaguṇodayam avandata tadā kṛṣṇo vāṅmanobuddhikarmabhiḥ
english: the great-souled one whose wrath is Time itself, in whom arise the powers of Śakra and Sūrya—him Kṛṣṇa then worshipped with word, mind, intellect, and deed.

sanskrit: yaṃ prapaśyanti vidvāṃsaḥ sūkṣmādhyātmapadaiṣiṇaḥ tam ajaṃ kāraṇātmānaṃ jagmatuḥ śaraṇaṃ bhavam
english: To Bhava, the unborn, whose essence is the cause, whom the wise perceive who seek the subtle station of the inner Self—to him the two went for refuge.

sanskrit: arjunaś cāpi taṃ devaṃ bhūyo bhūyo 'bhyavandata jñātvaikaṃ bhūtabhavyādiṃ sarvabhūtabhavodbhavam
english: And Arjuna too bowed before that god again and again, knowing him to be the one, the origin of what is and what shall be, the source of the becoming of all beings.

sanskrit: tatas tāv āgatau śarvaḥ provāca prahasann iva svāgataṃ vāṃ naraśreṣṭhāv uttiṣṭhetāṃ gataklamau kiṃ ca vām īpsitaṃ vīrau manasaḥ kṣipram ucyatām
english: Then Śarva spoke to the two who had come, as though smiling: "Welcome to you both, O best of men. Rise up, your weariness gone. And what is the desire of your hearts, O heroes? Tell it quickly."

sanskrit: yena kāryeṇa saṃprāptau yuvāṃ tat sādhayāmi vām vriyatām ātmanaḥ śreyas tat sarvaṃ pradadāni vām
english: "Whatever the purpose for which you two have come, that I shall accomplish for you. Choose what is for your own good, and all of it I shall grant you."

sanskrit: tatas tad vacanaṃ śrutvā pratyutthāya kṛtāñjalī vāsudevārjunau śarvaṃ tuṣṭuvāte mahāmatī
english: Then, hearing that speech, Vāsudeva and Arjuna, the two of mighty mind, stood up with hands joined in reverence and praised Śarva:

sanskrit: namo bhavāya śarvāya rudrāya varadāya ca paśūnāṃ pataye nityam ugrāya ca kapardine
english: "Homage to Bhava, to Śarva, to Rudra, and to the giver of boons; ever homage to the lord of beasts, to the fierce one, to him of the matted braid."

sanskrit: mahādevāya bhīmāya tryambakāya ca śambhave īśānāya bhagaghnāya namo 'stv andhakaghātine
english: "To Mahādeva, to the terrible one, to the three-eyed, to Śambhu, to Īśāna, to the destroyer of Bhaga—homage be to the slayer of Andhaka."
